Question #16For 3×33×3 matrices M and N, which of the following statement(s) is (are) NOT correct? (A) NTMNNTMN is symmetric or skew symmetric, according as M is symmetric or skew symmetric(B) MN-NMMN-NM is skew symmetric for all symmetric matrices M and N(C) MNMN is symmetric for all symmetric matrices M and N(D) (adjM)(adjN)=adj (MN)(adjM)(adjN)=adj(MN) for all invertible matrices M and N SolutionNTMNNTMN is symmetric or skew symmetric, according as M is symmetric or skew symmetricIf MT=MMT=M (symmetric)Let X=NTMNX=NTMN⟹X=NTMN⟹X=NTMN⟹X'=(NTMN)T⟹X'=(NTMN)T⟹X'=NTMTN=X⟹X'=NTMTN=X If MT=-MMT=-M (skew symmetric)XT=-XXT=-X⟹X=NTMN⟹X=NTMN⟹X'=(NTMN)T⟹X'=(NTMN)T⟹X'=-(NTMN)=-X⟹X'=-(NTMN)=-XHence, (A) is correct. Question #34Let P be matrix of order 3×33×3 such that all the entries in P are from the set {-1,0,1}{-1,0,1}. Then, the maximum possible value of the determinant of P is ___ Solution Trying to compute the maximum possible value Each row of the matrix can have at most three entries of 11. The length (magnitude) of such a row is 12+12+12=312+12+12=3 For a 3×33×3 matrix, the maximum possible determinant is the product of the lengths of the three rows: Max possible determinant=3×3×3=33≈5.19=3×3×3=33≈5.19 Next, narrow down the integer options Since the entries are integers {−1,0,1}{−1,0,1} the determinant must be an integer. The largest integer less than 5.195.19 could be 5 or45or4.det(P)≤5det(P)≤5. Now, Case 1: Matrix has at least one zero. If any row has a zero, its length ≤2≤2. Then:det(P)≤3×3×2=32≈4.24det(P)≤3×3×2=32≈4.24.So, det(P)≤4det(P)≤4. Case 2: Matrix has all entries ±1±1.For a 3×33×3 matrix with entires ±1±1, the maximum determinant is 4 (well-known result; can be verified by considering that dot products of distinct rows must be odd, so orthogonality is impossible).Therefore, 5 is impossible (in all cases) ∴det(P)≤4∴det(P)≤4Now, Check if 4 is possibleWe just need to see if we can actually get 4. It is a known fact that the matrix with all 1s on the diagonal and (-1)(-1)s elsewhere (or vice versa) gives 4.a
